title: Lazy-probe handoff routing with acceptance thresholds and rollforward fallback
creator: Aisha Martinez
description:
Summary:
We need a conservative, observable mechanism to try low-cost fast decode paths ("lazy probes") and seamlessly hand off to stronger decode paths only when the probe indicates likely failure to meet quality/time tradeoffs. This ticket specifies the routing policy, acceptance metrics, and a rollforward fallback strategy (progressive handoff to higher-capacity models/kernels) to reduce cost while protecting end-to-end quality and latency SLOs.

Goals:
- Reduce average per-token cost by serving a subset of traffic on aggressive fast-paths when acceptable.
- Keep tail latency (P95) within current SLOs for interactive workloads.
- Ensure graceful, observable handoffs and automated rollforward when probes indicate quality shortfalls.

Scope and approach:
1) Lazy-probe flow: spawn a short prefill or first-n token probe on a lightweight path (smaller model variant, lower-precision kernel, or reduced attention window). Probe must be non-blocking and have a tight time budget (configurable per route).
2) Acceptance metrics: define a compact decision vector computed from the probe result: per-token average log-prob ratio to baseline model (est. cross-model calibration), early-termination perplexity proxy, normalized confidence delta, and quick semantic similarity heuristic (embedding cosine between probe output and cached short-context baseline or a fast embedding model).
3) Acceptance thresholds: thresholds live in routing config with safe defaults. Decisions are probabilistic: probes produce an acceptance score; above threshold accept and stream probe result; below threshold trigger handoff. Thresholds should be tunable per-customer/route and have canary defaults that bias toward handoff until warmed.
4) Rollforward fallback behavior: if probe indicates low acceptance, route the request to a stronger decode path (larger model, full-precision kernels, full attention window). The rollforward should preserve partial outputs when possible (streaming stitch points) and avoid duplicated tokens in client-visible streams.
5) Observability and telemetry: emit probe_latency_ms, probe_compute_ms, acceptance_score, accepted:boolean, handoff_path, rollforward_reason, and quality_delta_estimate. Keep sample traces for offline calibration.

Design details:
- Probe budget: default prefill probe = 40ms compute, 125ms end-to-end (includes queue + preprocessing). Configurable by route.
- Probe modes: "micro-prefill" (single-token or up to 4-token probe generated with aggressive KV caching heuristics), "shallow-decode" (short decode with reduced beam/temperature constraints), and "kernel-fast" (same model but quantized kernel with smaller batch windows).
- Acceptance vector and weights (initial): logprob_ratio (0.4), early-perplexity-proxy (0.25), embedding-similarity (0.25), latency-margin (0.1). We will iterate weights based on calibration.
- Calibration harness: offline dataset with gold responses + traffic replay; compute ROC curve for acceptance score against quality delta (measured with rubric based on BLEU/ROUGE + semantic eval) and choose thresholds for target false-accept rate < 1% for P0 customer routes and < 3% for public routes.
- Safety: probes must never mutate customer data (read-only). When probe fails catastrophically (OOM, kernel crash), route immediately to fallback and mark probe as failed to avoid repeated retries.

Telemetry and SLOs:
- Target: sampled traffic using lazy-probe should show >= 12% unit-cost reduction without raising user-visible quality regressions above acceptance budget.
- Latency: end-to-end P95 should not increase by more than 10% for routes using probes. Probe tail errors must not increase overall error rate above 0.05%.
- Metrics to surface in Console: probe_accept_rate, probe_handoff_rate, avg_probe_latency_ms, avg_rollforward_latency_ms, quality_regression_rate, cost_unit_delta.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (internal): unit tests + calibration harness, run on synthetic traffic and compare to baseline (1 week).
- Phase 1 (canary): 1% of production traffic on non-critical routes, conservative thresholds, observe metrics for 2 weeks.
- Phase 2 (gradual): expand to 10% then 25% with route-specific tuning.
- Phase 3 (opt-in): expose routing knobs to Dedicated customers via Console.

Failure modes and mitigations:
- False accept (probe passes but quality suffers): include short-lived quality monitoring and automatic rollback if quality_regression_rate exceeds threshold.
- Probe instability (kernel crashes): circuit-breaker on kernel errors with exponential backoff.
- Streaming stitch conflicts: use token-idempotence window and per-request stream guards to suppress duplicate emission.

Test plan:
- Unit tests for acceptance score computation and threshold decisions.
- Integration tests: simulated reroute preserving token continuity, partial-output stitching.
- Load test: ensure probe budget does not induce queuing that increases tail latency unacceptably.
- A/B experiments: evaluate user-visible quality via offline evals and (where available) small-sample human-in-the-loop checks.

Migration and config:
- Default behavior off. Feature flag per-region/tenant.
- Expose probe mode, budgets, and thresholds via runtime config with per-tenant override.

Open questions:
- Should acceptance scoring be learned (model that predicts full-model acceptance) vs heuristic-based? Start heuristics, design extended API for model-based acceptors.
- How to best stitch streaming partials without increasing client complexity? Proposal: server-side stitch with explicit token anchors in stream protocol.

Acceptance criteria:
acceptance_criteria: Calibration harness produces ROC with false-accept < 1% for P0 routes at chosen threshold.
Probe_accept_rate and probe_handoff_rate visible in Console dashboards for canary routes.
A/B test shows >= 10% unit-cost reduction for sampled routes with quality_regression_rate below configured target.
End-to-end P95 latency increase <= 10% for routes with probes enabled.
Automated rollforward triggers and streaming stitch preserved in integration tests.
Security review completed (security_review_required = true) and all kernel sandboxing checks pass.
